drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna teach again that the majority of one siman in a bird renders the slaughter valid?
outcomeNote: The unit ends with the redundancy question; the answer falls outside this packet.

segments.he: רוֹב אֶחָד בָּעוֹף, תְּנֵינָא חֲדָא זִימְנָא: רוּבּוֹ שֶׁל אֶחָד כָּמוֹהוּ!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: If one cut «the majority of one» siman «in a bird» or the majority of two simanim in an animal,his slaughter is valid. The Gemara asks: «We» already «learn» this on «another occasion,» in the first clause of the mishna: The halakhic status of «the majority of one» siman «is like» that of the entire siman. Why is the redundancy necessary?
